hero.caption: Located in Pajaritos avenue, between Maipú and Ordóñez streets. This monument was constructed in memory of the soldiers patriots of the Army of the Andes, who conquered the Spanish Army, who had defeated the powerful Napoleon in Bailén's battle. It is necessary to emphasize that the General and Liberating Don Bernardo O'Higgins Riquelme was the one who designed and gave order to construct this monument.

images.caption:
Battle of Bailén 19 July 1808 : the defeated French army surrendered to General Castaños, Commander-in-Chief of the Spanish Army.  The negotiations took place at Villanueva de la Reina, about 10 km SW of Bailén, in the stage post (Casa de Postas, originally built in 1766), replaced since then by this present building (now a café-restaurant-pensión).  
It stands along the ancient road linking Granada to Cordoba (Madrid to Cadix), now the autovia A4/E5. 

Easily reached from either direction, but approaching it from Bailén, exit 310 km, provides the more striking view.

images.caption:
Architect Jacinto Higueras (1877-1954) received in 1909 his first significant order : a commemorative monument to two major battles fought in the Province of Jaén, which are illustrated on its socle : 
the 1212 Batalla de las Navas de Tolosa (on the West), and 
the 1808 Batalla de Bailén (<► File:Jaén – Monumento a las Batallas – Bailén 1808.jpg) (on the East).
A bronze statue of Athena-Nike, goddess of Victory, tops the column. 


The Monument was inaugurated on October 20, 1912.
